title: Rain
description: Rain in film is falling water that makes air visible as streaks and turns the ground into a mirror. Drops are matter in the optical path; without backlight they vanish, and without a wet-down the street stays dry under a fake storm.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Silver needles between a lamp and the lens. Shoulders darken.
Puddles double the neon. Weather is percussion you can see.
Make the air visible and the ground reflective. Use it when the scene must be wet in depth, not only on a window pane.
It is the wrong tool when you only need specular streets at night with no falling drops: that is a Wet-Down. It is also the wrong tool when you want a still veil that hides geography: that is Fog.
Rain against a bright overcast sky reads as nothing. Put a light behind the drops, toward camera, or lose the storm.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Put water in the air (rain bars, towers, or a real front) and light it from behind or the side so droplets scatter toward the lens. Keep a darkish background so streaks separate.
Wet the ground even if the rain is light. Shutter angle controls streak length versus beads.
Prompt: heavy rain around [Subject], backlit drops, wet-down pavement, umbrellas, silver streaks, weather as percussion.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it for a night street, a rooftop, a prison yard, any beat that needs falling water as a layer. Do not use it as a grade or as window tracks only.
If the air is empty and the asphalt is merely shiny, you shot a wet-down.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: A Wet-Down soaks surfaces so lights double; it need not rain. Atmospheric Haze is a distant scatter, not falling drops.
Snow is ice that settles and accumulates. Fog is a local veil that hides figures.
Rain falls, streaks when backlit, and leaves the ground wet.
Wet-DownNight exteriors that must sparkle.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: Blade Runner builds night as backlit rain and reflective streets. Seven uses rain as a constant layer over investigation.
The Shawshank Redemption lets a yard storm become a body-length release. Use drop, backlight, and wet ground, not a copied coat.

sections.title: Prompt it

blocks.text: Heavy rain around [Subject], backlit drops, wet-down pavement, umbrellas, silver streaks, weather as percussion. Name the backlight (a streetlamp, a sign, a HMI behind the rain), the wet ground, and drop size.
For video, falling streaks in depth, splashes, no dry asphalt. Do not write a mood word in place of the water.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is Wet-Down (shiny street, empty air) or a blue LUT called rain. The tell: no streaks against lamps, dry shoulders, no puddles.
The fix: put drops in the air, backlight them, wet the ground.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Rain in film?
Rain is falling water used as visible matter: backlit streaks in the air and reflective ground. Both the optical path and the pavement have to be wet.
Rain vs Wet-Down
A wet-down sprays surfaces so night lights specularize, often with no weather in the air. Rain adds falling drops. You usually wet-down under rain; you can wet-down without rain.
When should I use Rain?
Use it when air must streak and ground must mirror. Do not use it if you only need a shiny street, and do not expect rain to read against a bright empty sky without backlight.
How do I prompt Rain for AI image or video?
Name backlit drops and wet ground. Example: heavy rain around [Subject], backlit drops, wet-down pavement, silver streaks. Specify the lamp behind the rain and forbid dry asphalt.
